assumptions: The native code (C/Cython) build difference between buggy and fixed revisions is the sole determinant of whether division overflow is checked/raised vs silently saturating (i.e., not an environment-only numerical library difference).

The developer test T_dev is exactly pandas/tests/scalar/timedelta/test_arithmetic.py with the reproducing-test patch already applied in both revisions, and selecting -k test_td_div_float_ndarray_overflow will execute the intended overflow-raise assertion.

actions.step: Verify venv Python version for both revisions; rebuild only if needed so both runs use a compatible CPython matching upstream dev setup for compiled behavior.
Rebuild both revisions with compiled recipe to ensure C-extension code used by OutOfBoundsTimedelta path is correctly built for the transition test.
Run only the overflow-ndarray-float case from the specified file to force real failure/success transition.
Run the same single-case selection on fixed revision; expect it to PASS with OutOfBoundsTimedelta raised.

plans.success_criterion: On buggy revision the selected test -k test_td_div_float_ndarray_overflow fails with an assertion/exception mismatch corresponding to missing OutOfBoundsTimedelta (e.g., saturation value instead of raising). On fixed revision the same selection passes (OutOfBoundsTimedelta('Overflow in timedelta division') raised as expected), with no collection/import/setup error.
